item_name: TACTICAL TURNS DELAY 90°, DELAY 45°, IN PLACE, CROSS / HOOK / SHACKLE/ CHECK TURNS

observations.text: SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the delay 90 degrees turn geometry, did not exploit and convert the A/C energy in order to maintain position and did not check the corresponding responsibility airspace during the turn. Line abreast deviation reached 40 degrees and lateral separation deviated by 1400 feet, both beyond the code 1 tolerances of 30 degrees and 1000 feet. The IP directed the correction and flew part of the rollout to re-establish the tactical formation position.

SP, due to an unagreed division of lookout responsibility within the formation, did not apply the correction technique required to remain in tactical formation position during the delay 90 degrees turn. Line abreast deviation reached 30 degrees and the rollout was 30 degrees off the briefed recovery heading, at the code 1 tolerances. The turn was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP executed the delay 90 degrees turn within the desired standards, checking the corresponding responsibility airspace and rolling out in tactical formation position. Line abreast deviation twice reached 20 degrees and lateral separation deviated by 750 feet, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier energy management at the turn entry is expected to improve position keeping.

SP executed the delay 90 degrees turn as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, exploiting and converting the A/C energy in order to maintain position. Line abreast deviation remained within 8 degrees, lateral separation within 400 feet and the rollout within 6 degrees of the briefed recovery heading, without IP's intervention. Clearing and the responsibility airspace check were executed throughout the turn. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the delay 90 degrees turn with exceptional accuracy, taking the initiative for safe separation and rolling out precisely in tactical formation position. Deviations were negligible: line abreast within 3 degrees, lateral separation within 100 feet, recovery heading within 2 degrees and continuous G within 0.1 of the briefed value. The engine was used with consideration to the fuel reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not take initiative for safe separation during the delay 45 degrees turn and did not roll out in tactical formation position. Lateral separation deviated by 1400 feet from the briefed spacing and exit speed by 45 knots, both beyond the code 1 tolerances of 1000 feet and 30 knots. The IP intervened, directed the repositioning and flew part of the correction.

SP, due to a late and under-banked turn initiation, did not exploit and convert the A/C energy in order to maintain position during the delay 45 degrees turn. Exit speed deviated by 30 knots and altitude by 1000 feet high, at the code 1 tolerances. The tactical formation position was regained only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition of the energy deficit.

SP performed the delay 45 degrees turn within the desired standards, using the correction technique in order to remain in tactical formation position. Exit speed deviated by 22 knots and altitude by 650 feet high on two turns, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier power and pitch corrections at the turn exit are expected to improve.

SP executed the delay 45 degrees turn as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and rolled out in tactical formation position. Entry and exit speed remained within 10 knots, altitude within 200 feet and continuous G within 0.3 of the briefed value, without IP's intervention. The corresponding responsibility airspace was checked throughout the turn. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the delay 45 degrees turn with exceptional accuracy and precise energy management, rolling out in tactical formation position with negligible deviations. Exit speed remained within 4 knots, altitude within 80 feet and recovery heading within 2 degrees. The engine was used with consideration to the fuel reserve, and clearing with safe altitude for maneuvering over mountains was ensured throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the in place turn procedure and of the associated visual signals, did not execute the comm-out in place turn and did not check the corresponding responsibility airspace. Recovery heading was 45 degrees off the briefed value and line abreast deviation reached 45 degrees, both beyond the code 1 tolerance of 30 degrees. The IP directed the maneuver and executed part of the rollout to restore the tactical formation position.

SP, due to failure to pass a required call at the briefed point, did not initiate the in place turn in coordination with the leader and did not roll out in tactical formation position. Recovery heading deviated by 30 degrees and line abreast deviation by 30 degrees, at the code 1 tolerances. The turn was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts and the error was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP executed the in place turn within the desired standards and rolled out in tactical formation position. Recovery heading deviated by 18 degrees and line abreast deviation by 20 degrees on two repetitions, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - more precise timing of the turn initiation is expected to improve the rollout accuracy.

SP executed the in place turn as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, knowing and executing the visual signals in the comm-out turn. Recovery heading remained within 7 degrees and line abreast deviation within 8 degrees, without IP's intervention. Clearing and safe altitude for maneuvering over mountains were ensured throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the in place turn with exceptional accuracy, taking initiative for safe separation and checking the corresponding responsibility airspace throughout. Deviations were negligible: recovery heading within 2 degrees, line abreast within 3 degrees and lateral separation within 100 feet. The visual signals of the comm-out turn were given and answered without any prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position relative to the leader during the shackle, did not take initiative for safe separation and did not roll out in tactical formation position. Lateral separation deviated by 1500 feet and continuous G by 1.5 from the briefed value, both beyond the code 1 tolerances of 1000 feet and 1.0 G. The IP took the A/C to re-establish separation and directed the remaining cross turn.

SP, due to a mistimed hook turn initiation and an unstabilized bank, did not apply the correction technique required to remain in tactical formation position after the rollout. Recovery heading deviated by 30 degrees and lateral separation by 1000 feet, at the code 1 tolerances. The check turn was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition of the turn geometry error.

SP executed the cross, hook, shackle and check turns within the desired standards, checking the corresponding responsibility airspace during each turn. Recovery heading deviated by 20 degrees and lateral separation by 800 feet on the shackle, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the turn geometry across all four turn types is expected to improve.

SP executed the cross, hook, shackle and check turns as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and rolled out in tactical formation position after each one. Recovery heading remained within 8 degrees, lateral separation within 350 feet and continuous G within 0.3 of the briefed value, without IP's intervention. The visual signals were correctly given and answered in the comm-out turns. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the cross, hook, shackle and check turns with exceptional accuracy, exploiting and converting the A/C energy in order to maintain the tactical position throughout. Deviations were negligible: recovery heading within 2 degrees, lateral separation within 100 feet, line abreast within 3 degrees and continuous G within 0.1 of the briefed value. SP took initiative for safe separation and used the engine with consideration to the fuel reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.
